content.value_statement: Data teams need reliable checks before data reaches reports and products. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design validation suites, dbt tests, and data contracts.
actual_capabilities: Maps datasets to core quality dimensions such as completeness, validity, uniqueness, and freshness.
Drafts Great Expectations suites and checkpoint patterns for warehouse tables.
Designs dbt generic, singular, and model-level tests for analytics models.
Creates data contract structures with schema, quality, ownership, and SLA fields.
Plans automated validation workflows with alerts, reporting, and failure handling.
Recommends practical best practices for thresholds, ownership, and incremental adoption.
limitations: It provides implementation patterns, not verified rules for a specific production environment.
It cannot validate live datasets unless the user provides schemas, samples, and tool access.
Generated thresholds need review by data owners before deployment.
It does not replace privacy, compliance, or platform security review.

use_cases.title: Launch Warehouse Validation
use_cases.description: Create first-pass expectations for key warehouse tables before dashboards depend on them.

use_cases.title: Standardize dbt Testing
use_cases.description: Expand dbt model tests for uniqueness, relationships, freshness, accepted values, and business rules.

use_cases.title: Define Data Contracts
use_cases.description: Document schema, quality rules, ownership, and service levels for shared data products.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Quality Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a data quality plan for [dataset]. Include critical columns, quality dimensions, first checks, owners, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Validation Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate rule design for an existing table.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this table schema and sample values, propose Great Expectations checks and dbt tests with clear failure thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Contract
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced contract design for shared data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a data contract for [data product]. Include schema, quality rules, PII notes, owners, freshness, latency, and compatibility expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Framework
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit of an existing data quality program.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this data quality framework. Identify missing checks, weak thresholds, alerting gaps, ownership issues, and deployment risks.

output_examples.input: A user provides an orders table schema and asks for starter checks.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a prioritized validation plan with required fields, uniqueness checks, accepted statuses, freshness limits, and owner review notes.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to improve dbt tests for customer and order models.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests relationship tests, recency checks, accepted values, custom business rules, and a staged rollout plan.

output_examples.input: A data platform lead asks for a data contract outline.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines contract sections for schema, quality expectations, PII classification, ownership, service levels, and change management.

best_practices: Start with critical tables and columns before expanding to broad coverage.
Set thresholds with data owners and review failures before enforcing pipeline blocks.
Version data contracts and connect failures to clear remediation ownership.
anti_patterns: Do not block critical pipelines without alerting, fallback handling, and owner approval.
Do not hardcode thresholds without reviewing data volume, seasonality, and business context.
Do not publish validation reports that expose sensitive row values or personal data.

faq.question: What tools does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Great Expectations, dbt tests, data contracts, and automated data quality workflows.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready validation rules?
faq.answer: It can draft strong starting rules, but production thresholds need review with actual data and owner approval.

faq.question: Does it require live database access?
faq.answer: No. It can work from schemas, sample values, existing tests, or written requirements.

faq.question: Can it help with PII handling?
faq.answer: It can mark PII fields in contracts and advise safe reporting, but legal and privacy review may still be required.

faq.question: Is this useful for small teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports incremental checks that start with the most important datasets and expand over time.

faq.question: Can it review an existing data quality setup?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide current checks, schemas, and failure policies, and it can identify gaps and improvements.
